clue.text: Completely stop standard study after article rejected

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in 'up to par'

indicators.note: the article is thrown out of the word for study, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: to analyse something is to study it closely
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone abandons work on a standard after an article they wrote is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' looks like it describes the study, but it is what throws out the article.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something to a total halt, unable to move, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Commenter on web rebuked about large representative figure

parts.note: a poster is someone who posts comments online

indicators.note: the rebuke word wraps around the size letter

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to rebuke

explanation.surface: An online commenter is told off about a big public figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside CHID, an old past tense of chide.
explanation.definitionFit: A person held up as the typical example of a cause or quality is its emblem.

clue.text: Search all over, securing lecturer

indicators.note: the widespread word holds the lecturer letter fast inside it

parts.note: rife means widespread, found all over

explanation.surface: A search is made everywhere to get hold of a lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' puts L inside RIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through something is to ransack or rummage in it hunting for things.

clue.text: A lot of coffee I see in Italy in Italian glasses

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee
IC is text-speak for 'I see'
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Drinking plenty of coffee in Italy among Italian glassware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims LATTE to LATT. IC is how 'I see' is shortened in texts.
explanation.definitionFit: Venetian decorative glassware made with embedded threads of white glass, so a kind of Italian glass.

clue.text: Distressed a Parisian will abandon stupefying weapon

indicators.note: the French article leaves the weapon's name

parts.note: a stun gun stuns its target
un is French for 'a'

explanation.surface: A Parisian, upset, gives up a stun gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will abandon' takes UN out of STUNGUN, leaving STUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurt or upset by an unkind remark, as if pricked by an insect.

clue.text: Exclamation about working with US lawyer for 24 hours

indicators.note: the exclamation goes around the other pieces, wrapping them

parts.note: 'my!' is an exclamation of surprise
on means working or operating, as a machine is on
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: Someone cries out about working round the clock alongside an American attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: '24 hours' looks like part of the working scene, but it defines a whole day.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekday is a stretch of twenty-four hours, so any named day fits as an example.

clue.text: Old Paul from the Beatles mostly upheld historic philosopher

indicators.note: held up, so in a down clue the shortened nickname reads bottom to top
the nickname loses its last letter

parts.note: Macca is the nickname of Paul McCartney

explanation.surface: An aging Paul McCartney, largely respected, is compared to a medieval thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts MACCA to MACC and 'upheld' turns it to CCAM. Macca is the British tabloid nickname for Paul McCartney.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Ockham, the fourteenth-century English friar known for his razor principle.

clue.text: Aristocratic scientist's brother blocking degree over fabrication

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the next
the brother sits inside the degree abbreviation, blocking it

parts.note: a lie is a fabrication

explanation.surface: A noble scientist's brother obstructs a degree because of fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocking' puts BRO into DEG, and 'over' sets that above LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis de Broglie, French quantum physicist and Nobel laureate, held the title of duke.

clue.text: Ultimately they receive a positive vote

indicators.note: in the end, so the final letter of each of the next words is taken

explanation.surface: In the end they get a vote in favour.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for yes, used when counting votes for a motion.

clue.text: Beach reduced? Exclamation of annoyance about council's initial quick fix?

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the shore is the beach

indicators.note: the annoyed sound wraps around that letter

parts.note: tut is a click of disapproval

indicators.note: only the first letter of 'council's' is wanted

explanation.surface: A shortened beach draws a tut over the council's hasty remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a loose, playful one.
explanation.definitionFit: A quicker route also means a hasty method that skips steps, an expedient.

clue.text: Source of funds of that kind, frequently closed internally

indicators.note: the two short words sit inside the word for 'of that kind'

parts.note: such means of that kind, as in 'such people'
oft is an old word for often
a door pushed to is closed

explanation.surface: A source of money that is regularly shut off from within.
explanation.walkthrough: A door pulled 'to' is closed, a sense of the word the solver may not expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone easily persuaded to lend or give money is a ready source of cash.

clue.text: Horse beginning to rear when meeting a snake

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

indicators.note: only the opening letter of 'rear' is wanted

explanation.surface: A horse starts to rear up on meeting a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rear' looks like the horse's action, but only its first letter, R, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded venomous serpent of Asia and Africa, a kind of snake.

clue.text: Making things smooth again with words about border flower

parts.note: evening means levelling or smoothing out

indicators.note: the written words go round the border word

parts.note: prose is written words, as opposed to verse
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Smoothing things over with words about a flower in the garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' suggests a garden bed, but here it just means an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered plant whose blooms open in the late day, grown in gardens.

clue.text: Poles in valley uprising and French holding workers in servitude

indicators.note: the poles go inside the reversed valley word
rising up, so in a down clue the valley word reads upwards

parts.note: a vale is a valley
N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: the French word holds the workers inside it

parts.note: et is French for and
men are workers, a workforce

explanation.surface: Polish workers in a valley rise up with the French over forced labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns VALE to ELAV; 'in' puts NS into it; 'holding' puts MEN into ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Being held as a slave is the state of servitude itself.

clue.text: Dog seen beside river boat

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog breed

explanation.surface: A dog is spotted next to a river boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river boat' reads as one phrase, but 'river' gives R and 'boat' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship built to carry coal is called by the same name as a coal miner.

clue.text: Writing material: help in recording a period

indicators.note: the help word goes inside the record abbreviation

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
aid means help
per is an abbreviation for period

explanation.surface: Something to write on helps preserve a record of an era.
explanation.walkthrough: An LP is a long-playing vinyl record, hence 'recording'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper with a faint ribbed texture from the mould wires, used for letters and books.

clue.text: Recall one of the Engineers?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
one of a group is a member of it

explanation.surface: A question asking to bring back an army engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; one of them would be an RE MEMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something back to mind is to recall it.

clue.text: King? Both sides led by one in curtailed boardgame

indicators.note: the letters for one and both sides go inside the shortened game
cut short, so the game's last letter goes

parts.note: chess is a board game

indicators.note: the letter for one goes in front of the two sides

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a dog'
R and L are right and left, the two sides

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a king, set in a shortened chess game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both sides' means right and left; the shortened game wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Several British monarchs bear this name, so it stands for a king.

clue.text: One brought in weaponry with obligation to maintain constant truce

indicators.note: the numeral is taken into the weapons word

parts.note: arms are weapons
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the obligation holds the constant inside it

parts.note: a tie is a binding obligation
C is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Weapons are brought in under a binding agreement to keep a steady truce.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the physicist's constant, the speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreement between warring sides to stop fighting, as on 11 November 1918.

clue.text: I deliver iodine? I'm not sure — it's some kind of element

parts.note: to deliver from something is to rid of it
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
um is a sound of hesitation or doubt

explanation.surface: A chemist hesitates over whether to deliver iodine, unsure what element it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliver' suggests handing over, but here it means to free, RID.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard, dense metal of the platinum group, number 77 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Paint a period when there were no permanent workers?

definitions.meaning: a paint made by mixing pigment with egg yolk

definitions.text: a period when there were no permanent workers?
definitions.meaning: an age made up of temps, short-term staff, read as two words

explanation.surface: Depicting an age of casual labour, or a kind of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into TEMP ERA, an era of temporary staff; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-based medium used by painters before oils, still a type of artist's colour.

clue.text: Leave adviser circling street and head for empty shop

parts.note: to depart is to leave

indicators.note: the adviser surrounds the street abbreviation

parts.note: a mentor is a trusted adviser

indicators.note: only the first letter of 'empty' is taken

explanation.surface: An adviser walks round the street and heads for an empty shop before leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts ST into MENTOR to make MENTSTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A large retail store divided into sections selling many kinds of goods.

clue.text: Some writer on Donizetti identifying piece with recurrent theme

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is used, taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A music writer on Donizetti picks out a piece built on a returning tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical form in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

clue.text: Pacific nation's new sport bagging gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
RU is Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A Pacific country's new sport wins gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The sport is Rugby Union, abbreviated to its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny island republic in Micronesia, one of the world's smallest states.

clue.text: Arab resident soon upset

indicators.note: turned up, so in a down clue the phrase reads from bottom to top

parts.note: 'in a mo' means in a moment, soon

explanation.surface: An Arab resident will soon be upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IN A MO, informal for 'in a moment', upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or inhabitant of Oman, a sultanate in Arabia.

clue.text: Asian country sees censure after agreement in Germany

indicators.note: the censure word comes after the German yes

parts.note: ja is German for yes
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: An Asian nation is criticised after striking a deal in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: An island nation in East Asia, so it is one country on that continent.

clue.text: Bird very lucky to avoid Frenchmen

indicators.note: the word for lucky steers clear of the Frenchmen, dropping them

parts.note: jammy is British slang for very lucky
MM is short for messieurs, Frenchmen

explanation.surface: A very lucky bird dodges some Frenchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: JAMMY is British slang for lucky; MM is the abbreviation of messieurs.
explanation.definitionFit: A colourful crow-family bird, noisy and common in woodland.

clue.text: Cheer, having involved university investigators to explain

indicators.note: the cheer word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to elate is to cheer or delight
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Detectives brought in from a university explain the cause for cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: The investigators are the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something clear or throw light on it is to explain it.

clue.text: Recalled concern about a scented plant

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the letter A
called back, so the word for concern is read in reverse

parts.note: worry means concern or anxiety

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a worry over a fragrant plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns WORRY into YRROW, and 'about' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongly aromatic wild herb with flat white flower heads, also called milfoil.

clue.text: String player united a couple of quintets to appear in catalogue

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the catalogue word

parts.note: a list is a catalogue
U is an abbreviation for united, as in football team names
two fives make ten

explanation.surface: A string player brings ensembles together to feature in a concert catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quintets' suggests chamber groups but just means fives: two of them are TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the lute, a plucked stringed instrument.
